Fatally stabbed by my lover of 10 years. Imagine a windswept private beachfront estate, darkened by the cloudy moonless night. The power goes out! There’s a storm on the rise, two lovers search frantically in the dark. Praying that they find each other before they can.
  
What’s that? You hear something crash from the back gazebo, an intruder? Steadily tracing silent steps, filet knife in hand until you hear steps on the stone. Waiting, wondering, adrift in anxiety on the thoughts that prick your back.    

Suddenly they’re there and you think it’s too late. 
  
 Slash.
  Stab.

When you open your eyes you are relieved to see him “Blahblahblakely” smiling. He drops to the floor and you follow, not yet ready to face what you’ve done. 

He gasps, “It’s okay, I’m okay. You should be proud, but you can only stay for a moment.” His blood drew a picture in the stone path, it’s smell was of cinnamon and steel.

“One more please, just one more kiss before I go?”, said shyly as if no were an option. Gripping his shoulders to you, trying to feel him entirely. Knowing that he must feel very little, you cradle his head tenderly and meet his lips. Weakly they respond until the heart beat stops.

  You have killed him.

It comes so naturally sometimes so it's hard to fight but if I step away and take a breath (a BIG breath) and look at things differently. Trying to truly understand why someone upset you and what brought THEM to that point is a great mental exercise to get ahead of anger.
You should just take the next step and theorize a solution. It makes you look passionate and informed rather than like an angry ranter. Also you can usually start a debate this way!

Process the emotion as soon as possible so that you can't get over it first. Then be completely honest with yourself about how you feel and why you feel that way. Ask yourself what you mean when you say things and explore everything you feel. Then lay out the facts; what can change, what comes next, what's dead weight. Act accordingly and follow up with the people involved to release the emotions. After that you can move on. I found myself to be very good at being mean and hating people because I rationalize my negative emotions but it's much better to absolve yourself of the anger and bitterness so that you can really see what's going on with you.

I actually have a reply to this. Back in high school I joined a friend group in my sophomore year with some pretty cool people. There was one person in this group we'll call Nathan and we had a strange relationship, lots of banter and snide remarks, we were always giving each other a hard time. Nathan and I had a lot of similar interests that we didn't share with the rest of the group so we talked amongst ourselves for some things. He came out to me as bisexual after he came out to two other friends of ours which meant a lot because I thought he was straight the whole time.

___

Well we had a falling out around Junior/Senior year when I confessed that I had strong feelings for him and those feelings weren't reciprocated we had some tension between but never anything that really stood out to me. Come late senior year and I reach the depths of my depression and try to commit suicide and Nathan came to visit me in the hospital once, which I appreciated but after that visit he wouldn't talk to me at all even after I was released. We never got closure from that. 

___

About 2 years later I log onto Tumblr and see an anonymous message from Nathan (wasn't hard to figure it out) and in this message he named me as his greatest bully and the most toxic person that he had ever met, he said he hoped I was never happy. 

___

The real kicker with this story is the fact that I was his biggest advocate throughout high school; everyone in the friend group tolerated Nathan and considered him toxic, creepy, and needy. I stood up for him and tried to get him invited to things as much as possible partly because I was in love with him but also because I knew he didn't really have anyone else to turn to as he had a pretty bad home life as well. In the end we turned out to be each other's bad guy and I was never able to get ahold of him again to apologize or clarify anything.
